checkpoints: Compare Zustand to Context and Redux — understand the trade-offs
Create a store with state and actions
Use slices to organize large stores
Implement persistence with the persist middleware
Test a Zustand store in isolation

content.value: Zustand is a minimal, unopinionated state management library. Unlike Redux, there's no boilerplate — create a store with create(), define state and actions together, and consume with a selector hook. Slices keep large stores modular: create separate slice files and merge them in a root store. The persist middleware syncs state to localStorage automatically. For truly global, frequently mutating state (user sessions, shopping carts, notification queues), Zustand outperforms Context both in performance and developer experience. Benchmark your store selectors — fine-grained selectors prevent unnecessary re-renders.

checkpoints: Understand the difference between CSR, SSR, SSG, and ISR
Migrate a Vite React app to the Next.js App Router
Use Server Components vs Client Components correctly
Fetch data server-side with async Server Components
Implement dynamic routes and generateStaticParams

content.value: Next.js extends React with server-side capabilities. In the App Router (Next 13+), components are Server Components by default — they render on the server, reducing client bundle size and enabling direct database access. Add 'use client' only when you need browser APIs, event handlers, or hooks. Server Components can be async, so you can await a database query directly inside the component. ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) lets static pages revalidate in the background — the best of both static and dynamic worlds. This mental model shift from client-first to server-first thinking is the most important concept in modern React.

checkpoints: Set up Vitest and React Testing Library
Write unit tests for a pure utility function
Write integration tests that render components and interact with them
Mock API calls in tests with MSW (Mock Service Worker)
Achieve meaningful coverage on a feature without over-testing

content.value: Testing gives you the confidence to refactor and ship. React Testing Library's philosophy: test behavior, not implementation. Query elements by role or label text (getByRole, getByLabelText) — not by class name or component internals. Vitest is the test runner of choice for Vite projects. Mock Service Worker intercepts network requests at the service worker level, so your tests run against realistic API responses without hitting a real server. The testing pyramid: many unit tests for pure logic, integration tests for key user flows, and a few end-to-end tests with Playwright for critical paths like login and checkout.

checkpoints: Audit your app with axe DevTools and fix the top violations
Implement keyboard navigation and visible focus rings
Use ARIA attributes correctly for custom components
Test with a screen reader (NVDA or VoiceOver)
Integrate eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y into your workflow

content.value: Accessibility is not optional — it's a legal requirement in many jurisdictions and expands your audience. Use semantic HTML first: a <button> is already keyboard-accessible and announces correctly to screen readers; a <div onClick> is not. When you build custom components (dropdowns, modals, tabs), you must manage focus, keyboard events, and ARIA roles manually. The WAI-ARIA authoring practices document is the definitive reference. Use axe DevTools to catch violations automatically. Test with your keyboard only — if you can't reach and activate every interactive element, your app has accessibility bugs.

checkpoints: Understand when micro-frontends are worth the complexity
Set up Module Federation with Vite
Share a component library across two separate apps
Handle routing between micro-frontend shells
Discuss the operational trade-offs

content.value: Micro-frontends extend microservice thinking to the UI layer — different teams own different parts of the interface and deploy independently. Vite Plugin Federation implements Webpack Module Federation for Vite apps. A host (shell) app dynamically imports remote components from separately deployed apps at runtime. Shared dependencies (like React itself) are deduplicated via shared scope configuration. The trade-offs are real: independent deployability and team autonomy come at the cost of increased operational complexity, versioning challenges, and potential runtime errors if contracts break. Use this architecture only when team-scale and deployment independence genuinely demand it.

checkpoints: Measure Core Web Vitals in production with Chrome User Experience Report
Reduce LCP by optimizing image loading and server response
Eliminate layout shift (CLS) by reserving space for dynamic content
Use the React Profiler API programmatically to log render timings
Implement virtualized lists with TanStack Virtual

content.value: Real performance work is data-driven, not intuition-driven. Start with Core Web Vitals: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) measures loading, FID/INP measures interactivity, CLS measures visual stability. Use Lighthouse in CI to catch regressions. For long lists (1000+ items), virtualization is essential — TanStack Virtual renders only the visible rows, keeping the DOM small. The React Profiler API lets you log render timings in production: <Profiler id='ListView' onRender={callback}>. Ship a performance budget and treat violations like failing tests.

checkpoints: Plan a feature with a technical design document
Implement the feature using Next.js App Router with Server Components
Add full test coverage with Vitest and React Testing Library
Pass an axe accessibility audit with zero critical violations
Profile and document performance before and after any optimization
Write a short retrospective on decisions and trade-offs

content.value: Advanced mastery is demonstrated through production discipline, not just technical knowledge. Choose a non-trivial feature — an infinite-scroll feed, a real-time collaborative editor, or a multi-step checkout flow. Start with a design doc: what problem does it solve, what are the edge cases, what are the performance and accessibility requirements? Implement it with Next.js, test it thoroughly, and audit it for accessibility. The retrospective is mandatory: writing about your decisions cements learning and creates an artifact you can share with teams and interviewers.
